outcome: admission to special care neonatalogy unit
cohort: 585 primiparous and multiparous women aged 40 or above who delivered between January 2009 and December 2013 were compared to 1816 younger mothers aged 20 to 29 years.
finding: Advanced maternal age was associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery and several adverse perinatal outcomes, including preeclampsia/eclampsia, antepartum hemorrhage, fetal distress, fetal death, postpartum hemorrhage, preterm delivery, low birth weight, low Apgar scores, and perinatal mortality.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery rates were higher in both primiparous and multiparous women of advanced maternal age compared to their younger counterparts (38.5% vs 13.5% and 16.1% vs 9.1%, respectively).
birth_weight: Low birth weight was higher in older multiparous women (11% vs 7.7%).
